This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashment of FIR No.276/2022 registered in Police Station Kotwali, District Narsinghpur and all consequential proceedings.

2. It is contended by the counsel that applicant No.1 father-in-law (sasur), applicant No.2 brother-in-law(jeth), applicant No.3 sister-in-law (jethani) applicant No.4 sister in law (nand),
applicant No.5 brother-in-law (nandoi) and applicant No.6 sister-in-law (nand) of respondent No.2.
The marriage of respondent No.2 was solemnized with Mangal Singh Chouhan who is son of applicant No.1.
Unfortunately, Mangal Singh Chouhan died in road accident on 21/02/2022.
After death of Mangal Singh Chouhan, respondent No.2 started demanding her share in the property which was owned by applicant No.1 at Satna.

Respondent No.2 mounted undue pressure and also threatened the applicants that she would implicate them into a false NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:49955 2 MCRC-19482-2022 case.
Ultimately, respondent No.2 lodged the FIR against the applicants under Sections 498-A, 506 and 34 of IPC.
Assailing the said FIR and ensued proceedings, this petition has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants contends that the FIR prima faice does not contain any allegation regarding demand of dowry.

It is contended by the counsel that if entire FIR is perused Prakash Narayan Chouhan vs State Of M.P. on 27 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182277662/
1 carefully, the same would reveal that there is not a single allegation of demand of dowry at the behest of present applicants.

sentences.text: The FIR reflects that after death of husband of respondent No.2, the present applicants pressurized her to give all the money which belonged to her late husband and they also withdrew some amount from the account of her late husband.

The factum of transfer of fund from the account of respondent No.2's husband was informed by respondent No.2 to her brother, mother and maternal uncle(mama) and even they came to Satna where respondent No.2 was manhandlled by applicants.
It is contended by the counsel that the entire FIR contains no specific allegations against the present applicants and the same are general and omnibus.
It is further contended by the counsel that the applicant No.4, 5 and 6 who are not even residing at Satna have also been implicated.
Applicant No.4 is a resident of Jabalpur and applicant No.5 and 6 are resident of Kota, Rajasthan.

It is contended by the counsel that nowadays there is tendency to implicate the family members of the husband and accordingly following the said unfortunate tradition, the present applicants have been implicated.
Learned counsel thus submits that the proceedings deserves to be quashed.

4. To support his contention, learned counsel for the applicants NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:49955 3 MCRC-19482-2022 relied upon the judgments of Apex Court in the case of Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and Anr.

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submits that the petition deserves to be dismissed as there are direct allegations against the applicants.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that in the present case, conduct of the present applicants is required to be seen.

It is unfortunate that immediately after the death of husband of respondent No.2, the applicants siphoned off the entire amount which was available in the account of late husband of respondent No.2 and another FIR dated 18/05/2022 was lodged against applicant no.1 and 2 only.

It is contended by the counsel that specific details have been given in subsequent FIR dated 18/05/2022 which has been brought on record along with IA No.8532/2024 and as per the said allegation, even on the date of death of the husband of respondent No.2, money was withdrawn from the account of late husband of respondent No.2 and on subsequent occasions also, other amount was also withdrawn by applicant No.1 and 2.
It is therefore, contended by the counsel that there are being specific allegations against applicants, no case for interference is made out.

It is further contended by the counsel that demand of dowry is not an essential ingredient for the purpose of Section 498A IPC if the wife is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:49955 4 MCRC-19482-2022 subjected to cruelty that itself attracts the provisions of Section 498A of IPC,
hence, it is contended that the petition deserves to be dismissed.
7.
No other point is pressed or argued by the parties.

8. Heard rival submissions of the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: A perusal of the record reflects that the applicants have filed this petition seeking quashment of the FIR and the subsequent proceedings.

The FIR lodged on on 21/03/2022 contained in Annexure A/4 is reproduced as under:
                 
         13/12/2008         . 02
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:49955 5 MCRC-19482-2022 10.
A perusal of the aforesaid FIR reveals that so far as the demand of dowry is concerned, there are not a single allegation in the FIR.

The FIR if perused carefully, the same would reveal that after death of husband of respondent No.2, the present applicants mounted pressure upon respondent No.2 to hand over the amount and also to part with the other assets which were in the name of her late husband.

It was further mentioned that the amount from the husband's account was also transferred and when the brother, mother and maternal uncle of respondent No.2 came to Satna,
respondent No.2 was manhandled and then she came to Narsinghpur along with her mother and brother.
A perusal of entire FIR firstly does not contain specific allegations against the present applicants and no specific overt act of individual applicants has been explained in the FIR.
The allegations are undisputedly omnibus and general in nature.
The allegations precisely as regards parting with the money and assets which belonged to the late husband of respondent No.2.

If the said FIR is read simultaneously with subsequent FIR dated 18/05/2022 the same would reveal that in that FIR, same identical allegations have been leveled with specific details pertaining to Prakash Narayan Chouhan vs State Of M.P. on 27 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182277662/
3 withdrawal of amount of husband of respondent No.2.

The grievance of respondent No.2 is squarely covered by subsequent FIR dated 18/05/2022.
11.

So far as the FIR in question is concerned, undisputedly there are omnibus and general allegations against all the applicants and therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:49955 6 MCRC-19482-2022 the prosecution against them on the basis of such allegation is not permissible as has been laid down by the Apex Court in the catena of decisions.

Please see Kahakashan Kausar alias Sonam and others v. State of Bihar and others [(2022) 6SCC 599], Abhishek v. State of Madhya Pradesh [2023 LiveLaw (SC) 731], Preeti Gupta vs. State of Jharkhand (2010) 7 SCC 667 and Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and Anr.

12. The subsequent FIR dated 18/05/2022 lodged by respondent No.2 contains same allegations but with specific details and instances and implication in the subsequent report is specific detailing the specific attributed act of applicant No.1 and 2.
13.
In view of the aforesaid, this Court is of the opinion that so far as the impugned FIR dated 21/03/2022 is concerned, the same is unsustainable in view of omnibus and general allegations.
14. Accordingly, the FIR and ensued proceedings stands quashed.
The applicants stand discharged.
Their bail bonds if any, also discharged.
15. With the aforesaid present petition stands disposed of.
